note: XVII Paddington redrawn: period locomotive (Ian, 17 Nov).
style: A cinematic Romantic oil painting of 1893 in the manner of the reference: academic realism, atmospheric haze, shafts of light through steam, rich painterly brushwork, a wide establishing view. One single painting filling the whole 16:9 frame, no text, signature, border or black bars.

beats.text: Paddington Station, London, in 1893, seen from far down the platform: Brunel's great iron-and-glass train shed with its triple arched roof, shafts of grey daylight through drifting steam, and a Great Western express of the 1890s arriving: a slender single-driver locomotive with one huge driving wheel, a tall brass safety-valve cover, a polished brass dome, deep green paint with brown frames, a small four-wheeled tender, and a train of chocolate-and-cream carriages; porters, gas lamps, crowds in top hats and bustles, small and far off. No modern locomotive, no large boiler, no smoke deflectors.
